title: Health-Related Quality of Life and Experiences  of Home-Based Physiotherapy Among Older  Adults in Southern Portugal: An Exploratory  Mixed-Methods Study
content: Background/Objectives: Older adults with mobility limitations face barriers to outpatient rehabilitation. Home-based physiotherapy may improve access and support ageing in place, but evidence on recipients’ quality of life and experiences in Portugal is limited. This study described health-related quality of life and explored reasons for and experiences of using home-based physiotherapy among older adults in southern Portugal. Methods: This exploratory cross-sectional mixed-methods study included 30 adults aged ≥65 years receiving privately funded home-based physiotherapy. Health-related quality of life was assessed using the Portuguese SF-36v2. Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected, and non-parametric analyses were performed with Holm adjustment. Six participants underwent semi-structured interviews analysed using qualitative content analysis. Results: Mean age was 82.8 ± 7.9 years; 63.3% were women, 93.3% reported mobility difficulties, and 73.3% used an assistive device. The lowest mean scores were for Physical Functioning (18.67 ± 23.99) and Role Physical (27.50 ± 30.95); the highest were for Vitality (67.88 ± 12.41) and Mental Health (59.83 ± 14.47). Age correlated inversely with Physical Functioning (ρ = −0.391; raw p = 0.033). Interviewees cited transportation difficulties and valued accessibility, comfort, and individualised attention. Conclusions: This small convenience sample showed substantial limitations in physical functioning and role participation. Participants valued home-based care for reducing access barriers and enabling care in a familiar environment. The design does not support conclusions about treatment effectiveness.
